summary: @servicetitan/marketing-form ships preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executing 727 KB obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime (bun-v1.3.13) from GitHub releases into a temporary directory, extracts it (inlined ZIP parser with unzip/PowerShell fallbacks), chmods it executable, and then invokes the Bun binary against a sibling file math_init.js inside the package directory. math_init.js is a 727 KB single-line, heavily obfuscated blob using an array-rotation dispatcher (`WV8StW`) with a large numeric/string dictionary decoded by `hc1jfK9` and hex-mangled identifiers; it carries a `// @bun @bun-cjs` header indicating it is intended to run only under Bun, not Node. The library surface is a 78-byte re-export (`export * from './async-lazy-dropdown-state';`) that never references setup.mjs or math_init.js, so the install-time dropper is unrelated to the package's advertised React form-helper purpose. The alternate-runtime execution vector allows a payload authored for Bun's runtime to run on any machine that installs the package, regardless of whether Node would parse it, and evades tooling that only inspects Node-resolvable code. The package publishes under the `@servicetitan` scope but the install-time behavior does not match a form-helper library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
